problem: Prior VLN agents store memory in an unstructured LSTM hidden state. They have no geometric prior and no way to reason about the likelihood of alternative trajectories. To recover performance they fall back on physical search such as beam search, which yields trajectories hundreds to thousands of meters long. They also rely heavily on the simulator's navigation graph.
motivation: A navigation instruction can be read as a sequence of expected observations ('a bathroom', 'a coat rack near the stairs') and actions ('turn left') that a correct demonstrator would encounter and perform. Reasoning about alternative trajectories should therefore happen inside a map representation, where it costs no robot motion, rather than in the environment itself. The paper extends the Matterport3D simulator with depth so that a metric semantic spatial map can be used for VLN for the first time.
key_idea: Treat goal finding in VLN as Bayesian state tracking of a hypothetical human demonstrator (the 'ghost'). A differentiable histogram filter runs over a depth-projected semantic map, and its motion and observation models are conditioned on latent action and observation vectors decoded from the instruction.
insight: Explicitly modeling the whole trajectory as a recursive filter beats predicting the goal in one shot. The LingUNet baseline is essentially a single-step version of the model without the latent obs/action decoder and motion model. On val-unseen it reaches 32.2% average goal-prediction success versus 44.9% for the filter, and the filter wins at every time step, so the gain holds regardless of map sparsity. Adding heading θ to the filter state lifts success from 39.4% to 44.9%, which shows that relative orientation matters for grounding phrases like 'with the table on your left'. The attention visualizations show the two decoders specializing: the action/motion attention focuses on direction words and the observation attention on visual nouns. The full agent also barely overfits: SR is 34% on val-seen and 35% on val-unseen.
method: Depth-enabled Matterport3D simulator: renders cube-mapped depth from the MP3D undistorted depth images, fills holes with a cross-bilateral filter (NYUv2-style), and adds caching for up to 1000 FPS.

Mapper: frozen ImageNet ResNet-34 features (last 2 layers concatenated, 16x20x768) from 12 panoramic views are projected onto the ground plane using pooled depth, camera pose and a pinhole model, with max-pooling for cell collisions. They are integrated into a 128x96x96 world-frame map (0.5 m cells, 48 m x 48 m) by a sparsity-aware convolutional GRU with a masked update.

Instruction to latent observations/actions: a BiLSTM encoder (256 hidden, 300-d word embeddings) feeds an LSTM decoder driven only by a positional encoding of the step t. Two separate dot-product attentions produce o_t=[attended ctx, h_t] and a_t. The decoder runs a fixed T=6 steps, the maximum trajectory length in the navigation graph.

Histogram Bayes filter over the demonstrator state (x, y, θ): the belief starts at the known start pose. In the prediction step, a motion model convolves the belief with a kernel = softmax(3-layer CNN([a_t tiled, M])); the 7x7 kernel is upscaled 2x, allowing at most 3.5 m per step, and is map-aware for obstacles. In the observation update, the belief is multiplied elementwise by a discriminative 3-layer LingUNet(o_t, M) likelihood (sigmoid output, Θ channels) and renormalized. The filter is re-run from s_0 every time the map is updated.

Reactive policy: the global action space is all panoramic viewpoints observed so far, both visited and neighbors, and any of them can be reached in one action. Each viewpoint's logit is MLP([belief at t=1..T in a Gaussian neighborhood of the viewpoint, distance to it, visited flag]). Revisiting a viewpoint means STOP. The policy has no direct access to the instruction or the map.

Training: fully differentiable end to end except the CNN. The filter is trained with KL divergence between the belief b_1:T and the ground-truth demonstrator trajectory. The policy is trained with cross-entropy on the first shortest-path action, rolling out the policy's own action 50% of the time and the ground-truth action otherwise. Pure imitation learning with Adam (lr 1e-3, batch 5): 17.5K iterations for full VLN, about 2.5 days on one Titan X.

setting.backbone: ResNet-34 (ImageNet-pretrained, frozen) + ConvGRU mapper + BiLSTM/LSTM seq2seq instruction decoder + LingUNet observation model + CNN motion model + MLP policy (trained from scratch)
setting.training_data: R2R train split only (instruction-trajectory pairs), imitation learning; no RL, no data augmentation (no speaker/back-translation data), no specialized pretraining
setting.observation: panoramic RGB-D (12 views at 30° increments, 320x256, 60° VFOV, camera pitched 30° down) + camera poses; known intrinsics and ground plane
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoints (global action space over all viewpoints observed so far, including jumping to any previously observed viewpoint; revisit = stop)
setting.privileged: known camera/agent poses and rendered depth from the simulator (no GT map or semantics). The policy's action space uses the observed nav-graph viewpoints; mapper and filter do not use the nav graph.

results: On policy-free goal prediction, the filter with heading reaches 44.9% average success (<3m) and 4.67 m error on val-unseen. The LingUNet baseline gets 32.2% / 5.10 m and the hand-coded baseline 21.4% / 6.35 m, and the filter is better at every time step. On full R2R VLN it gets 35% SR / 31% SPL on val-unseen and 32.7% SR / 29.9% SPL on test with imitation learning only. That beats Speaker-Follower without augmentation (31% val-unseen SR) but trails Back Translation without augmentation (44% SR / 40% SPL) and SOTA methods using RL/augmentation (e.g. FAST 54% test SR). It shows almost no seen/unseen gap (34% vs 35% SR).
limitations: Full-VLN performance is well below contemporary methods (NE ~7.2-7.8 m vs ~5 m). The simple reactive policy has no access to the instruction or map, and it relies on the simulator's nav graph, including one-step jumps to any previously observed viewpoint.

Requires depth and accurate camera poses (from the simulator; SLAM would be needed in reality). The histogram belief is discretized (0.5 m cells, fixed 48 m map, Θ heading bins) and the filter always runs a fixed T=6 steps.
Trained only with imitation learning on R2R using a weaker ResNet-34; the checkpoint is selected on val-unseen SPL. RL and augmentation are left to future work.
